read_scope.pixel_inspection_reason: The session image channel returns image data with no readable text conclusion, so pixel viewing cannot serve as assertable evidence. Transcription fidelity below rests on the PDF text layer of both the reader and the source, checked with four deterministic instruments, one of which measures glyph sizes and baselines directly from the source page geometry.

preserved_literal_source_notation: Hypothesis, adjudication reading: the owner adjudication records the exercise as printing |A| < n^{d/2} and the Comment as printing |A| < n^d/2, keeps both literals, and notes that for n >= 2 the Comment's hypothesis is the weaker one so the exercise case is a subcase and the transfer is an inclusion, not a repair. This reader rewrites neither, and its p. 1 item on the hypothesis states both literals are transcribed exactly as printed.

Hypothesis, this task's own geometric measurement: measuring span sizes and baselines on the two source pages directly, physical p. 251 sets 'd' at 6.3 pt with baseline 170.3 against the solidus at 9.5 pt with baseline 174.2, and physical p. 637 sets 'd' at 6.3 pt with baseline 160.3 against the solidus at 8.4 pt with baseline 163.6. On both pages the exponent is raised and the solidus and the 2 sit on the baseline at body size, and the same-page control n^{1/3} on p. 251 has all three of its 1, solidus and 3 at 6.3 pt. So the printed form on both pages is n^d/2, and no page in the fixed source prints n^{d/2}. This reading is disclosed, is not used to overturn the adjudication's preservation of both literals, and no hypothesis is altered in this reader.

Attribution of the product bound: the Comment writes the product inequality as following from 'Theorem 6.22'. The statement printed under that name on physical p. 220 is |d_E A| >= 2d |A|^{(d-1)/d}; the product inequality prod_j |P_j(A)| <= |P_m(A)|^d is Lemma 6.23, printed on the same page and the lemma from which Theorem 6.22 is derived there. The printed attribution is kept verbatim and not corrected.
Wording of the set A: the exercise says A is 'a subgraph of the box', while the Comment writes A subset {0,...,n-1}^d. Both are kept as printed; no reading is imposed.
The constant: the exercise's C_d is not identified with the Comment's explicit (1-2^{-1/d}), and no small-n adjustment is inserted.

limitations: No pixel inspection of any page was performed; the conclusion rests on text layers and on geometric measurement of span sizes and baselines only. The three 150 dpi renderings under render/ are stored but were not viewed.

The PDF text layer of this source has systematic artefacts that a naive substring test misreads: Latin ligatures are decomposed ('de ned', 'su ces', 'in mum'), the sans-serif V of the vertex set is dropped, super- and subscripts are flattened, and the delimiter fonts encode \bigl\{ and \bigr\} as control code points 0x08 and 0x09. That single control character on reader page 3 is the Type1 delimiter font's encoding surfacing in extraction; it is not a missing glyph and not a rendering defect. The final instrument expands ligature code points and compares letter skeletons, which removes the first three without weakening the test.

Because super- and subscripts are flattened by extraction, exponent and index placement in the reader is not verified by these instruments; it is verified only insofar as LaTeX produced it and latexmk reported no error. The hypothesis-exponent question is therefore settled from the source page geometry, not from the reader's own extracted text.

The owner material review's honest_inputs names 'Loomis-Whitney as used by Theorem 6.22 on body p.221'; the printed page carrying both is physical p. 220 (printed p. 203), so that page reference is off by one. The owner report is not edited here; this reader cites physical p. 220, which is asserted against the source text layer.

The fixed source's printed record of the two hypotheses cannot be settled by letter-skeleton comparison alone, because the skeleton of n^{d/2} and of n^d/2 is identical. Both readings are therefore recorded above with the geometric evidence that distinguishes them, and the adjudication's preservation of both literals is left in force.
